answer: Whether agents trade ferrous scrap, forecast a gale, or manage an orchard, the market requires each active identity to lock 100 tokens in a public escrow contract, with a 30-day withdrawal delay. Each deposit backs only one identity at a time, so an attacker running 1,000 identities must immobilize 100,000 tokens. Creating names is free, but activating them consumes capital and sacrifices its use elsewhere; abandoning an identity cannot immediately recycle its stake.
